title: 2009 AMC 10A Problem 24
statement: Three distinct vertices of a cube are chosen at random. What is the probability that the plane determined by these three vertices contains points inside the cube?

solutions.text:
Three vertices determine a plane that cuts through the interior unless all three lie on a single face.

Each of the \(6\) faces gives \(\binom{4}{3} = 4\) triples, so \(6 \cdot 4 = 24\) triples lie on a face out of \(\binom{8}{3} = 56\) total.

The probability of hitting the interior is \[1 - \dfrac{24}{56} = \dfrac{4}{7}.\]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The plane avoids the interior exactly when all three vertices lie on one face
Count the same-face triples and subtract from the total \(\binom{8}{3}\)
